predecessors.name: Maurya Empire
predecessors.text: the Maurya heartland in its last year (the Gangetic remnant), Pataliputra and the plain around it

successors.name: Kanva dynasty
successors.text: the whole Shunga realm: 'The Kanva dynasty succeeded the Shungas around 73 BCE'; Cliopatria's Kanva shape of -66 has the same cells

successors.name: Satavahana dynasty
successors.text: Western and eastern Malwa, the Vidisha country, where 'the last remains of the Sunga state' were destroyed by the Andhras

ledger.x: 184 BCE: the Shunga dynasty is established at Pataliputra.
-91: the Shunga realm reaches towards the Sutlej.
73 BCE: the minister Vasudeva Kanva seizes the throne.

wars.name: Shunga-Indo-Greek wars
wars.outcome: 'Pushyamitra successfully completed the Ashvamedha Yagna' after a battle on the Sindhu river in which Vasumitra defeated Greek cavalry; the Indo-Greeks 'either led by Demetrius I or Menander I' invaded and Menander 'is credited with either joining or leading…

wars.name: Kharavela's campaigns against Magadha
wars.outcome: In his year 8 Kharavela's army 'laid siege to the city of Rajagriha' and in year 12 he 'subdues the king of Magadha'; the page does not name the Shunga and scholars disagree on the king's identity (Bahasatimita of Kaushambi and Magadha is one suggestion).

certainty.note: No frontier is dated or surveyed; the pages name capitals, viceroyalties and inscription findspots only.
